guides.titre: Senegal, told by the people who live there
guides.chapeau: A guide to travel the country with, an interpreter to be understood, and places whose history deserves to be told on the spot.
guides.heroAlt: A guide gives directions to two travellers in the city
guides.prestationsTitre: A guide, and not only for a tour
guides.prestationsTexte: You describe what you need, we look for the right person among our registered guides, and we send you a priced proposal that you accept or not.

prestation.accompagnementTexte: A guide who follows you from one region to the next, organises the stages, speaks to village chiefs and knows which road still works in the rainy season.
prestation.interpretariatTexte: For a business meeting, an administrative errand or simply the market: someone who moves between Wolof, French, English and Spanish without losing the meaning.
prestation.visiteGuideeTexte: A site guide who knows the history, the dates and the debates: Gorée, Saint-Louis, the Museum of Black Civilisations or a national park.
prestation.surMesureTexte: From half a day to two weeks, with or without a vehicle, as a family or a group. We build the programme with you before pricing it.

guides.languesTexte: Our guides work in French, English, Spanish and Wolof. For Arabic, Italian, Portuguese or German, tell us in advance: we will find someone, but we need a few days.
guides.equipeTexte: We only offer registered guides, whose references and status we verify before introducing them to you.
guides.prixTexte: No rate is displayed: it depends on the itinerary, the length and the number of people. You receive a priced proposal, and nothing is owed until you confirm it.
guides.tresorsTitre: Twelve places, and what to know about them
guides.tresorsTexte: From the island of Gorée to Niokolo-Koba, here is what our guides take you to see, with the history behind it and the advice a local would give you.
guides.carteNote: Approximate positions, at the village or the park entrance. They locate a site; they will not guide a vehicle.
guides.demanderPour: Request a guide for this site
guides.messagePour: I would like a guide for: {site}.

tresor.goreeAcces: 20 minutes by ferry from Dakar harbour
tresor.goreeHistoire: The Portuguese, Dutch, English and French fought over this eighteen-hectare rock for three centuries. The House of Slaves, built at the end of the 18th century, and its door opening onto the ocean made it the memorial of the Atlantic slave trade — historians debate how many captives actually passed through the island, never what it stands for today. Basalt lanes, the castel and the houses of the signares take half a day to walk.
tresor.goreeConseil: The last ferry of the evening fills up quickly: buy your tickets in the morning, and bring water — there is little shade on the island.
tresor.renaissanceAcces: 20 minutes from central Dakar, on the Mamelles hills
tresor.renaissanceHistoire: Forty-nine metres of bronze standing on a volcanic hill, unveiled in 2010 for the fiftieth anniversary of independence. Designed by the Senegalese architect Pierre Goudiaby Atepa and built by a North Korean workshop, the monument was argued over — its cost, its style, its figures — before becoming a landmark of the city. One hundred and ninety-eight steps lead to its base, a lift to the head of the man, from which the whole peninsula is visible.
tresor.renaissanceConseil: Go up late in the afternoon: the light is soft and the view reaches the Almadies.
tresor.civilisationsAcces: Central Dakar, near the Grand Théâtre
tresor.civilisationsHistoire: Opened in 2018, it carries out an idea Léopold Sédar Senghor had been pushing since the first World Festival of Negro Arts in 1966. Its rotunda unfolds the history of Black peoples, from the appearance of humankind in Africa to contemporary work, and its temporary exhibitions change several times a year.
tresor.civilisationsConseil: Allow two hours, and ask for a museum guide: the rooms are hard to read without someone to connect them.
tresor.lacRoseAcces: 35 km from Dakar, an hour by road
tresor.lacRoseHistoire: A lagoon far saltier than the ocean, where a micro-algae, Dunaliella salina, turns pink when the sun beats down and the water concentrates. The colour therefore ranges from lilac to red depending on the season, and in some years it does not come at all. The men of the lake have harvested its salt by hand since the 1970s, floating in a brine you cannot sink in. The Paris-Dakar rally long placed its finish line here.
tresor.lacRoseConseil: The pink rises around midday, when the sun is high. After heavy rain the lake can stay ochre: ask your guide how it looks before setting off.
tresor.bandiaAcces: 65 km from Dakar, an hour and a half by road
tresor.bandiaHistoire: Three thousand five hundred hectares of baobab forest fenced in 1990, where species that had disappeared from Senegal were reintroduced: white rhinos, giraffes, zebras, giant elands, buffalo and large antelopes. You cross it in a 4×4 with a tracker. Among the trees, a hollow baobab long served as a burial place for griots, and Serer burial mounds recall that people lived here well before the reserve.
tresor.bandiaConseil: Leave early: the animals show themselves in the cool hours and vanish into cover around midday.
tresor.saloumAcces: 150 km from Dakar, three hours by road
tresor.saloumHistoire: Five thousand square kilometres of sea arms, mangroves and bolongs, inscribed on the World Heritage list in 2011. Shell mounds built up over two millennia form entire islands here, and some carry Serer burial tumuli. At Fadiouth the village is built on shells, and its cemetery mixes Christian and Muslim graves on the same mound.
tresor.saloumConseil: The pirogue at dawn, between the mangrove roots: that is the hour of pelicans, herons and silence.
tresor.lompoulAcces: 150 km from Dakar, on the road to Saint-Louis
tresor.lompoulHistoire: Ochre dunes caught between the ocean and the savannah, the remains of an old erg that vegetation eventually surrounded. The place covers only a few square kilometres, which does not stop it from looking like the Sahara, and camps under Mauritanian tents let you sleep there far from any light.
tresor.lompoulConseil: A night on site changes everything: the sun falling on the crests, then a whole sky without light pollution.
tresor.saintLouisAcces: 270 km from Dakar, four hours by road
tresor.saintLouisHistoire: Founded in 1659 on an island in the river, it is the oldest French colonial town in West Africa. Capital of Senegal and then of French West Africa until 1902, it has kept its grid of streets, its houses with wooden galleries and the Faidherbe bridge — which earned it World Heritage status in 2000. Every spring the jazz festival fills the town.
tresor.saintLouisConseil: Cross over to the Langue de Barbarie early in the morning, when the Guet Ndar pirogues come back from fishing.
tresor.djoudjHistoire: Where the Senegal River meets the desert, sixteen thousand hectares of wetlands take in millions of migrating birds every winter, arrived from Europe after crossing the Sahara. White pelicans, flamingos, teals and spoonbills nest here in whole colonies. It is one of the leading bird reserves in the world, on the World Heritage list since 1981.
tresor.djoudjConseil: The season runs from November to April. Take the boat at daybreak, out to the pelican colony.
tresor.toubaAcces: 190 km from Dakar, three hours by road
tresor.toubaHistoire: The holy city of the Mouride brotherhood, founded in 1887 by Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba around the Great Mosque and its minaret. Each year the Grand Magal gathers several million pilgrims from across the country and the diaspora. The city lives by its own rules: no alcohol, no tobacco, no secular music.
tresor.toubaConseil: Cover shoulders and legs, headscarf for women. Your guide will tell you where you may enter and where you may not: it is asked, not guessed.
tresor.niokoloAcces: 650 km from Dakar, or a flight to Tambacounda
tresor.niokoloHistoire: Nine thousand square kilometres of wooded savannah along the Gambia river, inscribed on the World Heritage list in 1981. It is the last Senegalese refuge of the lion, the giant eland, the hippopotamus and the West African chimpanzee. Listed as in danger for years, the park came off that list in 2024 after its animal populations recovered.
tresor.niokoloConseil: Two days by road from Dakar, or a flight to Tambacounda. Only the dry season, December to May, is passable.
tresor.casamanceAcces: 450 km from Dakar, or an hour by plane
tresor.casamanceHistoire: South of the Gambia, another Senegal: rice fields, kapok forests, Diola impluvium houses and bolongs leading to the ocean. Ziguinchor and Cap Skirring are its gateways, and the villages of Lower Casamance are visited with a local guide — the only person able to explain the sacred woods and the place the king of Oussouye still holds.
tresor.casamanceConseil: Flying from Dakar avoids a long road and a ferry. The dry season, November to May, is the safest time to travel.

guides.demandeTitre: Tell us what you want to see
guides.demandeTexte: A few fields are enough. Our team finds the guide, puts the programme together and comes back to you with a priced proposal.
guides.faqQ1: Does the guide travel with us across the country?
guides.faqR1: Yes. An accompanying guide follows you from region to region for the agreed period. The vehicle and driver are requested separately, under Transport, and we match the two requests if you send them together.
guides.faqQ2: Can I have an interpreter without a tour?
guides.faqR2: Yes. A business meeting, an administrative errand, a hospital visit: say so in the message, it is a request like any other.
guides.faqR3: It depends on the itinerary, the length, the number of people and the language. That is why no rate is displayed: you receive a priced proposal, and nothing is owed until you confirm it.
guides.faqQ4: How far in advance should I ask?
guides.faqR4: Two days are enough for a visit near Dakar. Allow a week for a multi-day itinerary, Casamance or Niokolo-Koba, and more during the Magal and the Games.
guides.faqR5: We check the references and the status of every guide before offering them, and we only work with registered professionals.

restauration.chapeau: What people eat here, where the good tables are, how delivery works — and, if you prefer, a team that books for you.
restauration.heroAlt: Diners sharing several dishes around one table
restauration.platsTitre: Thirteen things to taste before you leave
restauration.platsTexte: Senegalese cooking is shared from one dish, simmered slowly, and runs from rice and fish all the way to tea poured three times. Here is enough to read a menu without hesitating.

plat.ceebuJenTexte: The national dish: rice cooked in a fish broth with tomato and vegetables — cassava, carrot, cabbage, bitter aubergine. Born in Saint-Louis in the 19th century, it is eaten at midday from one large bowl set in the middle. Inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2021.
plat.yassaTexte: Chicken or fish marinated in lemon and mustard, served under a mountain of slow-cooked onions. It comes from Casamance and pleases everyone, children included.
plat.mafeTexte: Meat simmered in a thick, mild peanut sauce, served over white rice. Filling enough that you plan nothing after it.
plat.soupouKandiaTexte: Pounded okra, palm oil and seafood over rice. Strong, a little slippery, genuinely good: this is what a Dakarois recommends to see whether you are serious.
plat.thiouTexte: A tomato stew with fish or meat, less famous than ceebu jën but on every neighbourhood menu.
plat.dibiTexte: Mutton grilled over wood, served on paper with onions and mustard, in dibiteries that open after dark. You eat with your fingers, standing or on a bench.
plat.chawarmaTexte: A legacy of Dakar's Lebanese community, settled here for a century. You find it on every corner, late at night, and it is often very good.
plat.pastelsTexte: Fritters stuffed with fish or meat, fried in front of you and dipped in spicy tomato sauce. The afternoon snack.
plat.accaraTexte: Black-eyed pea fritters served in bread with sauce. Street breakfast, for a few hundred francs.
plat.lakhTexte: Sweet millet porridge with curdled milk, eaten morning or evening. The ancestor of the Senegalese breakfast, before bread and butter.
plat.bissapTexte: The country's juices: tart red hibiscus, creamy baobab fruit, green and fragrant ditakh. Served iced and often very sweet — ask for less sugar if you need to.
plat.cafeToubaTexte: Coffee roasted with Selim pepper, which gives it its kick. Drunk standing at a tangana in the morning, for a hundred francs.
plat.atayaTexte: Green tea served in three successive glasses, from bitter to sweet, poured from high to raise the foam. A ceremony that lasts an hour: if you are offered it, someone has time for you.

restauration.usagesTexte: Nothing intimidating, but a few habits are worth knowing before the first meal.

usage.bolTexte: People often eat together from the same dish, each from the part in front of them, with the right hand or a spoon — one will be handed to you without asking. Your host will push the best pieces your way: that is attention, not a mistake.
usage.horairesTexte: Lunch is the real meal, around 2 pm, and it is generous. Dinner is late, rarely before 9 pm. In the morning people stop at a tangana for café Touba and bread and butter.
usage.terangaTexte: If you pass by at mealtime, you will be invited to eat. Declining three times is polite, declining forever is not — accept at least a few mouthfuls.
usage.ramadanTexte: Many places close during the day and reopen at sunset for ndogou, the breaking of the fast: dates, coffee, fritters. The whole country's timetable shifts; tell us if your stay falls in that period.
usage.regimesTexte: Meat is halal almost everywhere; alcohol and pork are only found in certain places, and never in Touba. Vegetarian takes planning: fish goes into nearly every broth, including those not named after it. Say so in advance and we will tell the restaurant.
usage.eauTexte: Drink bottled or filtered water. Good restaurants make their ice with treated water; on the street, hold off until you have acclimatised.

restauration.prixTexte: Orders of magnitude seen in Dakar, per person for a main course. They give you a sense; they do not commit any establishment.

prix.gargoteTexte: The neighbourhood dish of the day, served in a bowl. This is where everyone eats, and often where it is best.
prix.quartierTexte: A proper table, Senegalese or Lebanese menu, served at lunch and in the evening.
prix.bordDeMerTexte: Whole fish, lobster, a view of the ocean in Almadies, Ngor or Saly.

restauration.quartiersTitre: The neighbourhoods, and what you find there
restauration.quartiersTexte: Rather than a list of addresses that will be out of date in six months, here is the character of each area. Tell us where you are staying and we will look for the table of the moment — the one that is open and good that week.
restauration.carteNote: Approximate positions, at the centre of each area.
restauration.demanderPour: Find a table in this area
restauration.messagePour: I am looking for a table in this area: {quartier}.

quartier.plateauTexte: The administrative and business centre. Lebanese, French and careful Senegalese cooking, mostly at weekday lunchtimes. The Kermel and Sandaga markets are two steps away.
quartier.almadiesTexte: The westernmost point of Africa, and the evening tables: grilled fish, lobster, terraces facing the ocean. The most expensive part of town, and the one that dines late.
quartier.ngorTexte: Simpler and younger than Almadies: beach restaurants, the day's fish, pirogues crossing to Ngor island. Perfect at midday, feet in the sand.
quartier.pointETexte: The residential districts: bistros, world cooking, patisseries and long-established Senegalese addresses. This is where you eat well without paying for the view.
quartier.medinaTexte: Working, living Dakar: gargotes, dibiteries open at night, street grills. Local prices, everyday cooking, and plenty of people.
quartier.yoffTexte: A fishing village turned city district: the fish comes off the beach and is grilled a few metres away. The Virage tables open onto the ocean, ten minutes from the old airport.
quartier.diamniadioTexte: The Games hub: hotels, venue canteens and arena catering rather than neighbourhood tables. Worth knowing if you are staying there during the competitions.
quartier.salyTexte: An hour and a half from Dakar, the country's seaside resort: beach restaurants, French and Senegalese cooking, tables open late in season.

restauration.livraisonTexte: Three ways to have dinner without going out, in order of reliability in Dakar.
restauration.livraisonAppsTexte: They mainly cover Dakar and its near suburbs, and coverage varies from one area to the next: check your address in the app before relying on it. Payment is usually by Wave, Orange Money or cash on delivery.
restauration.livraisonWhatsappTexte: This is the most common method in the country, and often the fastest: the number is on the restaurant's Facebook or Instagram page, you send your order and address, and a rider sets off. Have small cash ready if you are not paying by Wave.
restauration.livraisonEquipeTexte: If you know neither the area nor the language, send us a request: we order, give the exact address and follow the delivery. It is the same form as for booking a table.
restauration.livraisonAvertissement: Delivery services appear and disappear quickly in Senegal: this list was checked in October 2026. Jumia Food, still recommended in places online, left the country at the end of 2022.

app.tiakTiakTexte: Meals, groceries and parcels in several cities, with rider tracking.
app.seneatTexte: Senegalese dishes and Dakar restaurants, payment by Wave or Orange Money.
app.dakarFoodTexte: A Dakar app: browse restaurant menus and have food delivered where you are.
app.livreurbiTexte: Dakar, Thiès and Saint-Louis, with cash on delivery available.
app.togalmaTexte: Office lunches delivered on weekdays, to be ordered the same morning.

restauration.demandeTitre: Tell us what you want to eat
restauration.demandeTexte: A table for tonight, a group dinner, catering for a birthday or a delivery to your accommodation: the team looks, books and sends you a proposal.
restauration.faqQ1: Can you book a table the same day?
restauration.faqR1: Often yes in Dakar, where few restaurants require a reservation during the week. For a Friday or Saturday night in Almadies, let us know the day before: the good tables are full.
restauration.faqR2: From eight people up, the restaurant needs warning — Senegalese cooking takes time and large dishes are not improvised. Allow two days, more during the Games.
restauration.faqQ3: I am vegetarian, coeliac or allergic. Is that workable?
restauration.faqR3: Yes, as long as you say so beforehand. Fish and peanut go into many preparations, including where you would not expect them. Put it in your request and we pass it to the restaurant in its own language.
restauration.faqQ4: Can we have food delivered to our accommodation?
restauration.faqR4: Yes, through an app or directly by the restaurant. If you would rather not deal with it, we order for you and follow the delivery to your door.
restauration.faqR5: The meal is paid at the restaurant, at its own price. Tell us your budget per person in the request: we look within that range rather than offering you a table out of reach.

assistance.titre: A team on the ground, for what you did not plan
assistance.chapeau: A form to get stamped, a medical appointment, a lost passport, an errand impossible to explain over the phone: you describe it, we take care of it.
assistance.heroAlt: An adviser wearing a headset reaching out a hand
assistance.domainesTitre: Nine situations we deal with every day
assistance.domainesTexte: The list is not closed. If your case is not on it, describe it anyway: that is exactly what this team is for.

domaine.accueilTexte: Someone waits for you at the exit with your name, helps with the SIM card and changing money, and takes you to your accommodation. Useful at 3 am, on a first arrival.
domaine.demarchesTexte: Certificates, permits, administrative appointments, collecting a document, accreditation: we know which counter, which hours and which paper is always missing.
domaine.santeTexte: Finding a doctor, a clinic or a duty pharmacy, making the appointment, driving you there and translating the consultation. For a life-threatening emergency, call the emergency services first.
domaine.traductionTexte: A phone call, a contract, a flat viewing, a conversation with a tradesman: someone moves between Wolof, French, English and Spanish, in person or on the phone.
domaine.documentsTexte: Police report, contact with your embassy or consulate, emergency travel document, replacing a bank card. We walk you through each step, in person if needed.
domaine.argentTexte: Opening a Wave or Orange Money account, finding a cash machine that works, changing currency without being cheated, understanding a quoted price. We never handle your money; we show you.
domaine.achatsTexte: Filling the fridge before you arrive, finding a spare part, buying a gift at the market at the right price, having something bulky delivered.
domaine.famillesTexte: Travel cot, car seat, a babysitter you can trust, a paediatrician, a pharmacy open at night. Family trips stumble on details, and details are settled in advance.
domaine.accessibiliteTexte: Checking that a place really is accessible, adapted vehicle, support at the Games venues, help with transfers. Tell us your needs precisely: we verify on site before confirming anything.

assistance.marcheTitre: From your message to the solution

etape.decrireTexte: In a few lines, in whichever language you like. The more precise — date, place, constraint — the faster the answer.
etape.reponseTexte: The team comes back with what it can do, how long it takes and the price, if there is one.
etape.referentTexte: One person follows your request from start to finish. You never explain your situation again to someone new.
etape.reglerTexte: Nothing is owed when you send the request. You pay for the service once it is done, on the spot, and never online.

assistance.delaisTexte: Support answers every day from 7 am to 11 pm, Dakar time. Outside those hours, your message is read when the team wakes up.

delai.urgenceTexte: Do not write, phone — or use WhatsApp. For a life-threatening emergency, the Senegalese emergency numbers come before us.
delai.jourTexte: An errand, an appointment, a formality: send the request and we come back within two working hours.
delai.prepareTexte: Airport welcome, medical support, family logistics: tell us two days ahead, more during the Games.

assistance.urgencesTexte: Fire, police, ambulance: in immediate danger, call the emergency services before writing to us.
assistance.demandeTitre: Tell us what is blocking you
assistance.demandeTexte: Describe the situation as it is. Even badly explained, even late at night, even if you think it is too small to bother us with.
assistance.faqQ1: Do I need to have booked accommodation with you?
assistance.faqR1: No. Support is a service in its own right: you can ask for it even if you are staying elsewhere, with relatives or in a hotel.
assistance.faqQ2: How much does an intervention cost?
assistance.faqR2: It depends on the time spent and the costs involved. Some things — advice, a number, pointing you the right way — are not charged. For the rest, you receive a priced proposal before anything starts.
assistance.faqR3: Yes, on the Petite Côte, in Thiès, Saint-Louis and Diamniadio without difficulty. Further away — Casamance, the east of the country — give us some notice, so we can activate someone locally.
assistance.faqQ4: Can you speak on my behalf on the phone?
assistance.faqR4: Yes. Many requests are settled by a call in Wolof that you cannot make yourself: give us the context and the number, we call and report back.
assistance.faqQ5: What if my request fits none of your categories?
assistance.faqR5: Send it. This service exists for cases no list anticipates; if we cannot help, we tell you straight away and point you elsewhere.

internet.titre: Connected in Senegal from the moment you land
internet.chapeau: How mobile works here, where to buy a local SIM, which operator to choose and what it really costs — without paying roaming rates.
internet.heroAlt: Two hands sliding a SIM card into a phone tray
internet.basesTexte: Forget the monthly contract taken from a bank account. In Senegal you buy a SIM for a few hundred francs, top it up with credit, and turn that credit into a pass: a volume of data valid for a day, a week or a month. When the pass runs out, you buy another. Nobody signs a contract and nothing renews itself.
internet.baseWhatsapp: The whole country communicates on WhatsApp: restaurants, drivers, landlords, sometimes administrations. A local SIM is therefore above all a Senegalese number on WhatsApp.
internet.operateursTitre: Three networks, and how to choose
internet.operateursTexte: All three cover Dakar properly. The difference shows beyond the city, and in the price per gigabyte.

operateur.orangeTexte: The country's leading network and by far the best coverage outside the cities: if you are heading to Casamance, the Saloum or towards Tambacounda, it is the safe choice. It is also the operator behind Orange Money, and the one with a desk at the airport.
operateur.orangeConseil: The sensible default, especially if you travel around the country.
operateur.freeTexte: The second network, often cheaper for the same volume and strong in Dakar and on the Petite Côte. Coverage drops off faster once you leave the main roads.
operateur.freeConseil: Good value if you stay around Dakar, Thiès and Saly.
operateur.expressoTexte: The third and smallest operator, with aggressive data promotions. Uneven network depending on the district; best kept for a short, urban stay.
operateur.expressoConseil: Worth a look as a backup or a second SIM.

etape.papiersTexte: Identification is compulsory in Senegal: no SIM is activated without an ID registered in the user's name. A passport is enough. Refuse a SIM already registered to a stranger, even to save time: it can be cut off overnight, and you are responsible for whatever goes out from it.
etape.boutiqueTexte: An operator branch or an approved dealer — there is one in every district, and at the airport on arrival. Street sellers offer the same SIMs for less, but without valid registration or any recourse if something goes wrong.
etape.identificationTexte: The seller scans your passport and registers the line. It takes a few minutes, in front of you. Check that the SIM works before leaving the shop: a call, a text, a web page.
etape.passTexte: The SIM alone gives you almost nothing. Ask for a data pass matching your stay — a few gigabytes for a week is plenty if your accommodation has wifi. Offers change often: ask to be shown the current passes in the shop rather than trusting a price read online.
etape.rechargeTexte: Through the operator's app, a USSD code, any shopkeeper displaying the logo, or from Wave and Orange Money. Credit is sold everywhere, including on a Sunday evening.

internet.simPrixTexte: Orders of magnitude, to be checked at the counter: the SIM itself costs a few hundred francs, a few gigabytes for a week runs into the thousands of francs, and the tourist pack sold at the airport costs noticeably more than a SIM bought in town — you are paying for convenience on arrival.

couverture.dakarTexte: 4G everywhere, fast, including on public transport. 5G has existed since 2024 but remains limited to certain areas: do not build anything on it.
couverture.villesTexte: Decent 4G in town centres and along the main roads. The Games venues are well covered but saturate when the crowd arrives — plan not to depend on the network to find each other.
couverture.brousseTexte: 3G, sometimes nothing at all. Orange reaches where the others no longer do. Download your maps offline before leaving, and warn your family that you will be unreachable at times.

option.esimTexte: Bought online before departure and activated on landing, it runs on the local networks. Handy on day one, but a gigabyte costs several times the price of a local pass: a good stopgap, a poor plan for three weeks.
option.roamingTexte: Senegal is outside the zone of almost every European plan: roaming is charged at full rate. Turn data off on arrival and check your international option before touching it.
option.wifiLogementTexte: Most places listed here have fibre or a 4G box. Ask about the real speed before booking if you have to work, and plan a backup: cuts happen.
option.boxPortableTexte: A small 4G router with its own SIM, connecting several devices. Useful for a group or on the move, and one of the options we can prepare before you arrive.

internet.conseilsTitre: Four things to settle before you leave

conseil.telephoneDebloqueTexte: A handset locked by a foreign operator will not accept the local SIM. Check before departure: it cannot be sorted out here.
conseil.doubleSimTexte: With dual SIM or an eSIM, keep your usual line for bank codes and apps, and put the data on the Senegalese SIM.
conseil.waveTexte: Mobile payment is everywhere: a local number lets you open a Wave or Orange Money account and pay for a taxi, an errand or a meal without cash. You need an ID, the same one as for the SIM.
conseil.whatsappTexte: If you move WhatsApp to your Senegalese number, your contacts will no longer recognise you. The simplest is to keep WhatsApp on your usual number and use the local SIM for data.

internet.demandeTitre: We can take care of it
internet.demandeTexte: A local SIM registered in your name, an eSIM, a wifi box: tell us what you need and where you land. The team prepares it, delivers to the airport or your accommodation, and you leave connected.
internet.messagePour: I would like a {operateur} SIM card.
internet.faqQ1: Can I buy my SIM at the airport on arrival?
internet.faqR1: Yes, the operators have desks there and registration is done on the spot with your passport. It is the easiest option on arrival, but the tourist packs cost more than a SIM bought in town the next day.
internet.faqQ2: Will my phone from home work?
internet.faqR2: Yes if it is unlocked: the 2G, 3G and 4G bands used in Senegal are the same as in Europe. A handset locked by your operator will refuse the local SIM, and that is unlocked before you travel, not after.
internet.faqQ3: How much data should I plan for?
internet.faqR3: For a normal stay with wifi where you sleep, a few gigabytes a week is enough: maps, messaging, social media. If you work on video calls or share your connection, count double and take a monthly pass.
internet.faqQ4: Can I keep my Senegalese number after the trip?
internet.faqR4: A prepaid line stays active as long as it is used, then is deactivated after several months without a top-up. If you come back every year, a small top-up now and then is enough to keep it.
internet.faqQ5: How good is hotel and rental wifi?
internet.faqR5: It varies. In town, fibre is common and decent; elsewhere it is often a 4G box shared between several flats, with power cuts that take the internet down too. A local SIM is the right insurance.

q.compte: How do I create an account on Teranga Way?
q.compteR: Select “Create account” at the top of the site, then enter your name, your email address and a password of at least 10 characters. We email a six-digit code to that address: enter it and your account is ready. You do not need an account to browse the site — it is only asked for when you send a request.
q.delai: How quickly does the partner reply?
q.delaiR: Usually within the hour for a place to stay. If nobody replies within two hours, the request expires and we offer you something else.
q.paiementR: Sending a request triggers no payment. After acceptance, depending on the service, Teranga Way may ask you for a deposit, to be paid by bank transfer or Mobile Money using only the details in the email it sends you. It only counts once our team has checked that it was received, and it does not by itself confirm your booking: only the status of your request does. A partner cannot ask you to pay a deposit outside this procedure. The rest is paid on site, directly to the partner (cash, Wave or Orange Money depending on the partner). We never ask for a bank card.
q.prix: Can the price change after my request?
q.prixR: No. The price is fixed the moment you send your request.
q.adresse: Why is the address not shown?
q.adresseR: The exact address and the partner's contact details appear after you confirm. It protects you as much as them.
q.annuler: Can I change or cancel my booking?
q.annulerR: Yes, from your request details. The partner's cancellation terms are on every listing before you send.
q.refus: What happens if my request is declined?
q.refusR: We immediately offer you other places available on the same dates.
q.deuxHeures: Why can't I book a ride straight away?
q.deuxHeuresR: Arranging a pick-up takes two hours. For an immediate need, call the team: they will find a way.
q.reserver: How do I make a booking?
q.reserverR: Pick a place or a vehicle, give your dates and send a request. The provider replies within two hours. Nothing is confirmed — or held — until they accept.
q.contacter: How do I contact a provider?
q.contacterR: Their contact details reach you once the request is accepted, not before. Until then, write from the request itself: your message gets through without either of you sharing a number.
q.securiteR: We only ask for what the booking needs: name, phone, email. The platform neither asks for nor stores any bank card; a deposit, if any, is paid by bank transfer or Mobile Money to Teranga Way's details only. If you are a provider, your supporting documents are not stored here.
q.probleme: What should I do if something goes wrong during my stay?
q.problemeR: Call support: it is the quickest way. For a medical emergency, the police or a fire, dial the emergency numbers directly — they are listed on the Emergencies page.
q.avis: How do I leave a review after my stay?
q.avisR: A review can only be left once a stay is over, from your account. That is what guarantees the reviews you read come from people who really stayed.
q.devenirPrestataire: How do I become a provider on Teranga Way?
q.devenirPrestataireR: Create a provider account in five steps. Our team calls you back, checks your supporting documents off the platform, then publishes your listing. Allow 24 to 48 hours.

epopee.poleDakarTexte: The heart of the Games, with the Iba Mar Diop Stadium, the western Corniche and Dakar bay.
epopee.poleDiamniadioTexte: Abdoulaye Wade Olympic Stadium, Dakar Arena and the Athletes' Village.
epopee.poleDiamniadioAcces: 35 min by motorway or the TER
epopee.poleSalyTexte: Water sports, sailing and triathlon on the Petite Côte.
epopee.compteAReboursTexte: The best places go quickly. Plan your stay ahead.

demandeTransport.volAide: If you are heading to or from the airport, so we can track your flight.
demandeTransport.messagePlaceholder: Hello, I would like to book this vehicle. Could you confirm it is available?
demandeTransport.aucunPaiement: No payment when you send. A day with a driver may involve a deposit after acceptance; trips and taxis are paid to the driver on the spot.
demandeTransport.coordonneesApres: The driver's name and number reach you once the request is confirmed.
demandeTransport.delaiReponse: The partner replies within an hour.
demandeTransport.envoyeeTexte: You will get an answer by email and in your account.
demandeTransport.delaiTropCourt: Pickup must be requested at least two hours in advance. Please choose a later time.

resultatsTransport.aucunResultatTexte: Widen your criteria, or call the team: they will find one.
resultatsTransport.carteEtiquette: Map of the areas served by transport

ficheVehicule.apercuTexte: Travel in comfort and safety with an experienced driver. They meet you on arrival and know the routes to the Games venues.
ficheVehicule.confirmationRapideTexte: You get an answer from the provider by email and in your account, within an hour.
ficheVehicule.avisBientot: Reviews on vehicles will arrive with the first trips.

panne.titre: Something went wrong on our side
panne.texte: We could not load this page. Try again in a moment.
panne.appeler: If it happens again, call the team: {telephone}.

demandeService.intro: Describe what you need. Our team finds a checked provider and sends you a quote, which you accept or not.
demandeService.pasDeCatalogue: This service has no online catalogue yet: the team searches for you.
demandeService.messagePlaceholder: Anything that helps us search well: constraints, preferences, accessibility…
demandeService.envoyeeTexte: The team looks for a provider and replies within 24 hours, by email and in your account.
demandeService.aucunPaiement: No payment now. You will be quoted a price before committing to anything.
demandeService.echecTexte: Try again in a moment. If it happens again, call the team.

inscription.texte: An account lets you track your requests and book without re-entering your details.
inscription.motDePasseAide: At least {longueur} characters. A phrase is safer and easier to remember than a complicated word.
inscription.dejaInscrit: This address already has an account. Sign in to continue.
inscription.verificationTexte: We sent a six-digit code to {email}. It is valid for ten minutes.
inscription.codeRenvoye: A new code has just been sent.
inscription.attenteExpiree: Your registration has expired. Please start again.
inscription.confirmationErreur: The two passwords do not match.
inscription.motDePasseCourtErreur: Too short: at least {longueur} characters are required.
inscription.sousTitre: Create your account and get your stay ready.

acompte.sousTitre: Manual payment: nothing counts as received until a person has checked the account.
acompte.inactif: Deposits are not enabled: no payment is requested from visitors.
acompte.aucunDossier: No deposit is open for this request.
acompte.ouvrir: Open the deposit and send instructions
acompte.reste: Still to receive on the deposit
acompte.tardif: A payment arrived after the deadline: decide whether to accept it or return it, after review.
acompte.offreDejaConfirmee: Another confirmed request already occupies this offer on overlapping dates: no deposit is opened and no payment instructions are sent.
acompte.offreDejaConfirmeeOuverture: No deposit was opened: another confirmed request already occupies this offer on the same dates.
acompte.surplus: The amount received exceeds the expected deposit by {surplus}. Partial refunds are not supported here: the excess is handled outside this screen, and no refund is made automatically.

decisions.aucunTransfert: This screen transfers no money and promises the customer no timeframe: it records decisions and refunds made outside the platform.
decisions.limites: A refund always covers the whole amount received. Returning only a part or an overpayment is not supported by this screen. No refund timeframe is announced to the customer.
decisions.examen: What was checked (availability, request still alive…)
decisions.dejaRembourse: I made this refund myself, outside the platform. This screen does not do it.

acompte.coordonnees: Configured payment details (those of future emails)

reception.exact: This amount matches what is still due.
reception.avertissementInferieur: {manque} will still be missing: the deposit stays partial and the booking not final.
reception.avertissementSuperieur: This amount exceeds what is due by {surplus}. No refund is made automatically.
reception.ecartConfirme: I acknowledge this difference and record it as is.
reception.verifie: I have checked that the funds were actually received on the bank or Mobile Money statement. A customer's claim or a screenshot is not enough.

envoi.echec: The email could not be sent: the record is up to date, you can resend it.
envoi.sansDestinataire: No email address on the customer's account: nothing was sent.
envoi.nonRequis: No email needed to be sent.

erreur.ecart: The amount differs from what is due: acknowledge the difference and add a comment.
erreur.concurrent: The record changed in the meantime (another validation or a double click). Nothing was recorded: reload it.
erreur.doublon: This transaction reference is already recorded on this record.
erreur.nonAttendu: This deposit no longer awaits payment.
erreur.demandeClose: The request is closed: no receipt can be recorded on it.
erreur.rienAConfirmer: No receipt is recorded: nothing to resend.
erreur.serveur: The server could not process the request.
erreur.rienARembourser: There is nothing to refund on this deposit.
erreur.nonARembourser: No refund is decided on this deposit.
erreur.montantRemboursement: The refund covers the whole amount received; partial refunds are not supported.
erreur.pasEnRetard: This deposit has no late payment to decide.
erreur.incomplet: The payment is not complete: it can only be returned.

admin.connexionTexte: Enter your team account's address. A six-digit code is waiting there.
admin.codeEnvoye: If that address is known, the code has just been sent. It expires in ten minutes.
admin.erreurAdresse: That email address is not valid.
admin.erreurEnvoi: The code could not be sent: the API has no email service configured. Locally, set AUTORISER_COMPTES_DEMO=true and the code will be shown here.
admin.erreurTropDeCodes: Too many codes requested. Wait a minute before trying again.
admin.erreurRole: The account {email} has no access to the back office. Check the address, or have it added to the team.
admin.erreurServeur: The server did not answer. Try again in a moment.
admin.serveurTexte: The back office reads requests straight from the API. Check that it is running and that the site points to it, then try again.
admin.avertissementMock: The back office needs the real API. While NEXT_PUBLIC_API_MOCK is not set to false, team sign-in cannot open.
admin.avertissementSession: Session expired or access denied. Sign in again with your team address.
admin.noteInterneAide: Seen by the team only, never by the visitor or the partner.
admin.prixProposeAide: For a service without a catalogue: the amount the team quotes.
admin.prestataireIdAide: Pick a partner from the list, or none to detach.

coordonnees.sousTitre: Entered by the team and checked by another person before the visitor can see them.
coordonnees.nonPrevues: No contact details are planned for an on-demand service.
coordonnees.nonSaisissables: Contact details can be entered and checked while the request is accepted or confirmed — not once the service is over, nor after a cancellation, expiry or refusal.
coordonnees.avertissementRessaisie: Saving new contact details cancels the check: another person will have to check them again.
coordonnees.attenteAutre: Awaiting a check by another team member: the person who entered them cannot check them.
coordonnees.enregistrees: Contact details saved. Another person must now check them.
coordonnees.erreurQuatreYeux: You entered these details: another team member must check them.
coordonnees.erreurConflit: The request or its details changed in the meantime. Reload the page before trying again.
coordonnees.erreurStatut: The request's status does not allow this operation.
coordonnees.erreurDejaVerifiees: These details have already been checked.
coordonnees.erreurARessaisir: These details must be entered again before they can be checked.
coordonnees.erreurMigration: This feature is waiting for the database update that records who enters and who checks.
coordonnees.erreurSession: Your session does not allow this operation. Please sign in again.
coordonnees.erreurServeur: The server did not respond. Try again in a moment.

admin.dernieresDemandesTexte: The six most recent, whatever their status.
